```{ojs}
data = FileAttachment("dashboard/data.json").json()
```

```{ojs}
// Colour is assigned by the entity it names, never by rank or order.
ORIGIN_COLOR = new Map([["real", "#2a78d6"], ["simulated", "#eb6834"]])
TIER_ORDER = ["high_priority_cross_study", "multi_omics_convergence", "emerging"]
TIER_LABEL = new Map([
  ["high_priority_cross_study", "High-priority cross-study"],
  ["multi_omics_convergence", "Multi-omics convergence"],
  ["emerging", "Emerging (needs replication)"]
])
TIER_COLOR = new Map([
  ["high_priority_cross_study", "#1c5cab"],
  ["multi_omics_convergence", "#2a78d6"],
  ["emerging", "#86b6ef"]
])
origin = (d) => (d.simulated ? "simulated" : "real")
fmt = (n) => (n == null ? "—" : n.toLocaleString("en-US"))
fmtP = (p) => (p == null ? "—" : p < 1e-3 ? p.toExponential(2) : p.toFixed(3))
phen = (id) => data.vocab.phenotype_labels[id] ?? id
stress = (id) => data.vocab.stressor_labels[id] ?? id
k = data.kpis
plotWidth = Math.max(360, Math.min(820, width))  // `width` is Observable's reactive container width
missing = Object.entries(data.artifacts_present).filter(([, v]) => !v).map(([n]) => n)
```

```{ojs}
missing.length
  ? html`<div class="callout callout-style-default callout-warning"><div class="callout-body-container callout-body"><p>
      <strong>Pipeline outputs missing from this build:</strong> ${missing.join(", ")}.
      Counts that depend on them read as zero below. Run <code>make demo</code> (and the real-study
```

::: {.callout-note}
Every number on this page is derived from files in the repository at the commit above: study YAMLs under `registry/studies/`, the harmonized evidence table, the meta-analysis and candidate tables, the git log, the test suite, and the candid [implementation status](implementation_status.md) page. **Simulated demo studies are always separated from real studies**, here and in every AREE pooling and ranking step. A high candidate score is an association across the evidence AREE has, not a validated biomarker.
:::

## What the evidence currently says

```{ojs}
{
  const realClasses = data.candidates.by_evidence_class.filter(d => !d.simulated);
  const total = realClasses.reduce((s, d) => s + d.n, 0);
  const realPools = data.pools.filter(p => !p.simulated);
  const classText = realClasses.length
    ? realClasses.map(d => `<strong>${fmt(d.n)}</strong> ${d.evidence_class.replace(/_/g, " ")}`).join(", ")
    : "no ranked real candidates yet";
  const poolText = realPools.length
    ? realPools.map(p => `<em>${phen(p.phenotype)}</em> / ${p.feature_type}: ${p.studies.join(" + ")}, ${fmt(p.n_features_k2plus)} features pooled from ≥ 2 studies, ${fmt(p.n_features_k2plus_significant)} of them with BH-adjusted p ≤ 0.05`).join("; ")
    : "no real cross-study pool has formed yet";
  const gap = k.n_real_comparisons_with_resilience_phenotype === 0
    ? "No registered real comparison measures a resilience outcome, so AREE cannot yet produce <em>resilience-associated</em> evidence from real data."
    : `${k.n_real_comparisons_with_resilience_phenotype} of ${k.n_comparisons_real} real comparisons carry a resilience-classed phenotype; whether it enters a pool depends on the source reporting a standard error.`;
  return html`<p>Across ${fmt(total)} ranked real candidates the evidence class breaks down as ${classText}.
    Pools formed on real data: ${poolText}.</p>
    <p>${gap} Every real study registered so far is an RNA-seq pathogen-challenge experiment, so the ranked list is
    dominated by disease-associated transcriptional responses. Adding a second stressor class and a study with a
    measured survival or pathogen-load phenotype is the highest-value next curation step
    (see <a href="candidate_studies.html">candidate studies to curate</a>).</p>`;
}
```

### Top-ranked real candidates

Ranked by tier (hard gates), then transparent score. Gene symbols and descriptions come from the committed NCBI/UniProt crosswalk; "uncharacterized" is NCBI's own annotation, not a gap in AREE's mapping. Click a feature ID to open its evidence card, which lists every contributing study and the limitations.

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(data.candidates.top_real, {
  columns: ["feature_id_standardized", "gene_symbol", "gene_description", "phenotype_label", "tier",
            "evidence_class", "score", "k_studies", "total_sample_size", "pooled_effect",
            "adjusted_p_value", "direction_consistency", "i_squared"],
  header: {feature_id_standardized: "Feature", gene_symbol: "Symbol", gene_description: "Description",
           phenotype_label: "Phenotype", tier: "Tier", evidence_class: "Evidence class", score: "Score",
           k_studies: "k", total_sample_size: "n", pooled_effect: "Pooled effect (log2FC)",
           adjusted_p_value: "BH-adj. p", direction_consistency: "Direction consistency", i_squared: "I²"},
  format: {
    feature_id_standardized: (v, i, rows) => rows[i].card_page
      ? htl.html`<a href="${rows[i].card_page}">${v}</a>` : v,
    tier: v => TIER_LABEL.get(v) ?? v,
    evidence_class: v => v.replace(/_/g, " "),
    score: v => v.toFixed(1),
    pooled_effect: v => (v == null ? "—" : v.toFixed(2)),
    adjusted_p_value: fmtP,
    direction_consistency: v => (v == null ? "—" : v.toFixed(2)),
    i_squared: v => (v == null ? "—" : `${(v * 100).toFixed(0)}%`)
  },
  rows: 15, width: {gene_description: 240}, layout: "auto"
})
```

### Ranked candidates by tier and origin

```{ojs}
{
  const rows = [];
  for (const o of ["real", "simulated"]) for (const t of TIER_ORDER) {
    const hit = data.candidates.by_tier.find(d => origin(d) === o && d.tier === t);
    rows.push({origin: o, tier: t, n: hit ? hit.n : 0});
  }
  return Plot.plot({
    marginLeft: 200, height: 220, width: plotWidth, style: {background: "transparent"},
    x: {label: "Ranked candidates", grid: true, tickFormat: "~s"},
    y: {domain: TIER_ORDER, tickFormat: t => TIER_LABEL.get(t), label: null},
    fy: {domain: ["real", "simulated"], label: null},
    color: {domain: ["real", "simulated"], range: ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834"], legend: true, label: "Origin"},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(rows, {x: "n", y: "tier", fy: "origin", fill: "origin", rx: 3, insetTop: 2, insetBottom: 2,
        tip: true, title: d => `${TIER_LABEL.get(d.tier)}\n${d.origin}: ${fmt(d.n)}`}),
      Plot.text(rows.filter(d => d.n > 0), {x: "n", y: "tier", fy: "origin", text: d => fmt(d.n),
        dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fill: "#0b0b0b"}),
      Plot.ruleX([0])
    ]
  });
}
```

The simulated column is a pipeline demonstration and includes the deliberately planted cases (an imperfect identifier mapping and a conflicting-direction gene). It is shown so the demo can be checked against the design, not as a finding.

```{ojs}
{
  const rows = data.evidence.by_study.map(d => ({...d, origin: origin(d)}))
    .sort((a, b) => (a.origin > b.origin) - (a.origin < b.origin) || b.n_records - a.n_records);

    marginLeft: 170, height: 40 + rows.length * 26, width: plotWidth, style: {background: "transparent"},

      Plot.text(rows, {x: "n_records", y: "study_id", text: d => fmt(d.n_records), dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fill: "#0b0b0b"})
```

### Comparison-level pipeline status

Each registered contrast, whether its standardized result table exists in the repository, whether it has been harmonized into the evidence table, and whether it is the one contrast a study nominates for cross-study pooling (`meta_analysis_primary`). Unharmonized real comparisons are work still to be done.


### Identifier mapping confidence

How the original identifiers in each origin resolved against its crosswalk (synthetic for simulated studies, real NCBI/UniProt for real studies). `unresolved` is preserved, never dropped or guessed.

```{ojs}
{
  const order = ["exact", "one_to_one_ortholog", "one_to_many_ortholog", "many_to_one_ortholog", "inferred", "unresolved"];
  const rows = data.evidence.mapping_confidence.map(d => ({...d, origin: origin(d)}));
  return rows.length ? Plot.plot({
    marginLeft: 150, height: 260, width: plotWidth, style: {background: "transparent"},
    x: {label: "Evidence records (log scale)", type: "log", grid: true, tickFormat: "~s"},
    y: {domain: order.filter(o => rows.some(r => r.mapping_confidence === o)), label: null},
    fy: {domain: ["real", "simulated"], label: null},
    color: {domain: ["real", "simulated"], range: ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834"], legend: true, label: "Origin"},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(rows, {x: "n", y: "mapping_confidence", fy: "origin", fill: "origin", rx: 3, insetTop: 2, insetBottom: 2,
        tip: true, title: d => `${d.mapping_confidence} (${d.origin}): ${fmt(d.n)}`}),
      Plot.text(rows, {x: "n", y: "mapping_confidence", fy: "origin", text: d => fmt(d.n), dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fill: "#0b0b0b"})
    ]
  }) : html`<em>No evidence table in this build.</em>`;
}
```

### Simulated demo candidates

Kept separate from real candidates on purpose. These come from the six synthetic demo studies and exist so that the pipeline's behavior (including a planted conflicting-direction gene and an imperfect identifier mapping) can be checked against the design.

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(data.candidates.top_simulated, {
  columns: ["feature_id_standardized", "phenotype_label", "tier", "evidence_class", "score", "k_studies",
            "total_sample_size", "adjusted_p_value", "direction_consistency", "mapping_confidences"],
  header: {feature_id_standardized: "Feature", phenotype_label: "Phenotype", tier: "Tier", evidence_class: "Evidence class",
           score: "Score", k_studies: "k", total_sample_size: "n", adjusted_p_value: "BH-adj. p",
           direction_consistency: "Direction consistency", mapping_confidences: "Mapping"},
  format: {
    feature_id_standardized: (v, i, rows) => rows[i].card_page ? htl.html`<a href="${rows[i].card_page}">${v}</a>` : v,
    tier: v => TIER_LABEL.get(v) ?? v, evidence_class: v => v.replace(/_/g, " "),
    score: v => v.toFixed(1), adjusted_p_value: fmtP,
    direction_consistency: v => (v == null ? "—" : v.toFixed(2))
  },
  rows: 10, layout: "auto"
})
```

## How this page is built

1. The Pages workflow (`.github/workflows/pages.yml`) installs AREE, registers every study in `registry/studies/`, harmonizes the simulated studies against the demo crosswalk and the real studies against the real crosswalk, runs the meta-analysis and candidate ranking, and then runs `aree build-dashboard`.
2. `aree build-dashboard` writes `docs/dashboard/data.json` and copies the evidence cards for the top-ranked candidates beside it.
3. `quarto render docs` renders this page from that JSON and the site is deployed to GitHub Pages.

Locally, `make dashboard` does the same after `make demo`. The JSON and copied cards are generated, not committed.
